newsitem.title: USA: Human remains found at Arizona jet crash site.
newsitem.headline: Human remains found at Arizona jet crash site.

text.p: Rescue crews searching for an Air Force pilot missing from a crashed A-10 Thunderbolt attack aircraft found "fragmentary human remains" on Wednesday, the Air Force said.

But officials at Davis-Monthan Air Force base in Arizona refused to confirm whether they were the remains of Capt. Amy Lynn Svoboda, who was on a routine training mission from Davis-Monthan when her single-seat fighter crashed.
The remains were to be taken to the Air Force Institute of Pathology for positive identification, said the officials who could not say when the results would be available.

Svoboda's plane crashed on Tuesday night during an exercise at the Barry Goldwater Training Range in southwest Arizona. The Air Force said the A-10, designed to destroy tanks and other armour, was carrying a variety of practice weapons.

The crash was the second involving an A-10 from Davis-Monthan in almost two months. In April, Capt. Craig Button, 32, inexplicably left his four-aircraft formation and veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles away (1360 km) from a training exercise.
Button's plane crashed into a snow-covered mountain peak and it was more than three weeks before a rescue team was able to recover his body.
